It is the Abushina Shrine listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha}} of {{ill|Mino Province|ckb|پارێزگای مینۆ|cs|Mino (provincie)|de|Provinz Mino|es|Provincia de Mino|eu|Mino probintzia|fa|ولایت مینو|fr|Province de Mino|gl|Provincia de Mino|hak|Mî-nùng-koet|id|Provinsi Mino|it|Mino (provincia)|ja|美濃国|ko|미노국|lt|Mino žemė|nl|Mino (provincie)|pt|Província de Mino|ru|Мино (провинция)|simple|Mino Province|sk|Mino (provincia)|sr|Провинција Мино|th|แคว้นมิโนะ|tr|Mino (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Міно|vi|Tỉnh Mino|wuu|美濃国|zh|美濃國|zh_min_nan|Mino-kok|zh_yue|美濃國|qid=Q864156}}{{ill|Kamo District, Gifu|ceb|Kamo-gun (distrito sa Hapon, Gifu-ken)|es|Distrito de Kamo (Gifu)|fr|District de Kamo (Gifu)|id|Distrik Kamo, Gifu|it|Distretto di Kamo (Gifu)|ja|加茂郡|ko|가모군 (기후현)|pl|Powiat Kamo|pt|Distrito de Kamo|th|อำเภอคาโมะ|uk|Повіт Камо (Ґіфу)|vi|Kamo (quận)|zh|加茂郡|qid=Q1348656|lt=Kamo District}}.

It is located about 200 meters south of {{ill|Kawabe Ōhashi Bridge|ja|川辺大橋|qid=Q11479293}}.

Every year on April 13–14, the annual festival (Abushina Shrine Festival) is held. On the 13th, during the Shigaraku Festival, one {{ill|Matsuri float|Q11470974|qid=Q11470974}} is pulled. On the 14th, during the Honraku Festival, the Fly-Chasing Man (said to represent {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|Q3090037|qid=Q3090037|lt=Sarutahiko-no-Mikoto}}) chases children while holding a {{ill|Cleyera japonica|Q775470|qid=Q775470|lt=sakaki branch}}, and it is said that if he strikes their backs, they will enjoy good health and freedom from illness for that year.

=== Overview ===
The shrine is said to have been founded in {{ill|Kōnin (era)|de|Kōnin (Ära)|es|Kōnin (era)|fa|کونین (دوره)|fr|Ère Kōnin|ia|Konin (era)|id|Kōnin|ja|弘仁|ko|고닌|ru|Конин (нэнго)|simple|Kōnin (era)|sr|Конин (ера)|tr|Kōnin (dönem)|uk|Конін (ненґо)|zh|弘仁|zh_yue|弘仁|qid=Q1373070}} 9 ({{ill|818|Q25083|qid=Q25083}}). Its original location was about 700 meters north of the current site. After being relocated in {{ill|Jōgan|Q1075635|qid=Q1075635|lt=Jōgan}} 1 ({{ill|860|Q24714|qid=Q24714}}), it was moved to its present location in {{ill|Kanpyō (era)|Q1346292|qid=Q1346292}} 9 ({{ill|897|Q30468|qid=Q30468}}).

During the {{ill|Edo period|Q184963|qid=Q184963}}, it was known as “Afukai Myōjin” and “Haga Tennō.” In {{ill|Meiji era|ar|فترة مييجي|ast|Dómina Meiji|az|Meydzi dövrü|azb|مئی‌جی دؤورو|be|Перыяд Мэйдзі|bn|মেইজি যুগ|bo|མེའི་ཇིའི་དུས་དུས་མཚམས།|ca|Era Meiji|cs|Období Meidži|da|Meiji-perioden|de|Meiji-Zeit|el|Μεϊτζί (περίοδος)|es|Era Meiji|et|Meiji periood|eu|Meiji Aroa|fa|دوره میجی|fi|Meiji-kausi|fr|Ère Meiji|gl|Período Meiji|he|תקופת מייג'י|hr|Meiji (razdoblje)|ht|Epòk Meiji|hu|Meidzsi-kor|id|Zaman Meiji|io|Ero Meiji|is|Meiji-tímabilið|it|Periodo Meiji|ja|明治|ka|მეიძის ეპოქა|kbp|Mejii wɛɛ yaa alɩwaatʊ|kk|Мэйдзи дәуірі|ko|메이지 시대|la|Aetas Meiji|lt|Meidži laikotarpis|lv|Meidzi periods|mk|Меиџи (период)|mn|Мэйжийн эрин|ms|Zaman Meiji|nl|Meijiperiode|nn|Meiji|no|Meiji-perioden|pl|Meiji (okres)|pt|Era Meiji|ro|Perioada Meiji|ru|Мэйдзи|simple|Meiji period|sk|Obdobie Meidži|sq|Periudha Meixhi|sr|Меиџи период|sv|Meijiperioden|ta|மெய்சி காலம்|th|ยุคเมจิ|tl|Panahong Meiji|tr|Meiji Dönemi|uk|Період Мейдзі|ur|میجی دور|vi|Thời kỳ Minh Trị|war|Panahon Meiji|wuu|明治|zh|明治|zh_classical|明治|zh_min_nan|Bêng-tī|zh_yue|明治|qid=Q3125096}} 6 ({{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}}), it became a {{ill|Gō-sha|ja|郷社|qid=Q134917316}}.
